 WNBA Atlanta Dream v Golden State Valkyries: WNBA finals 2026 Game 7 – live updates
 Valkyries host Dream in winner-take-all Game 7
 Both teams are seeking first WNBA championship
 Reach out to Bryan on Bluesky or by email 
 LIVE  Updated  13m ago Bryan Armen Graham Sat 31 Oct 2026 21.12 EDT First published on Sat 31 Oct 2026 19.08 EDT Share Key events 18m ago Half-time: Dream 30-24 Valkyries 
 47m ago End of first quarter: Dream 11-12 Valkyries 
 1h ago Tonight’s starting lineups 
 2h ago How they got here 
 2h ago Preamble 
 Atlanta’s Angel Reese drives to the basket against Golden State’s Kiah Stokes during the first quarter of Saturday night’s winner-take-all Game 7 of the WNBA finals at Chase Center in San Francisco. Photograph: Ezra Shaw/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Atlanta’s Angel Reese drives to the basket against Golden State’s Kiah Stokes during the first quarter of Saturday night’s winner-take-all Game 7 of the WNBA finals at Chase Center in San Francisco. Photograph: Ezra Shaw/Getty Images Bryan Armen Graham Sat 31 Oct 2026 21.12 EDT First published on Sat 31 Oct 2026 19.08 EDT Share Key events 18m ago Half-time: Dream 30-24 Valkyries 
 47m ago End of first quarter: Dream 11-12 Valkyries 
 1h ago Tonight’s starting lineups 
 2h ago How they got here 
 2h ago Preamble 
 14m ago 21.11 EDT No one has been a bigger handful for the Golden State defense in the first half than the 5ft 6in Canada , who has repeatedly knifed her way into the paint and created opportunities for Atlanta.
 “Just being aggressive, doing what I do best,” Canada told USA’s Meghan McPeak. “I know I can get into the paint. I know that’s one of my strengths, so I’m just trying to get there as much as I can.”
 Canada, who scored nine of Atlanta’s last 11 points before the intermission, also stressed the importance of turning defensive stops into transition opportunities.
 “When we get stops and then we get out in transition, that’s when we’re at our best.”
 View image in fullscreen Atlanta’s Jordin Canada scored a game-high 13 points in the first half of Game 7. Photograph: Ezra Shaw/Getty Images Share Updated at  21.12 EDT 18m ago 21.07 EDT Half-time: Dream 30-24 Valkyries
 Twenty minutes into the first Game 7 in WNBA history, points are at a premium and Atlanta have a six-point advantage.
 Jordin Canada has carried the Dream offensively with 13 points, including 11 in the second quarter, as Atlanta outscored Golden State 18-10 in the period. Angel Reese has five points and seven rebounds, while Rhyne Howard has been held to just two points on 1-of-7 shooting.
 The box score is a particularly grim look for the Valkyries, who shot just 21.4% in the second quarter and are 9-of-30 (30%) overall, including a frigid 1-of-11 from three-point range. Veronica Burton is pacing the hosts with eight points but has missed eight of her 11 shots. Gabby Williams has managed just two points on four attempts, although she has contributed three of Golden State’s six blocked shots.
 Perhaps the most telling statistic: Atlanta have a 12-3 edge in second-chance points, making the most of their opportunities in a game where clean looks have been scarce.
 Share 28m ago 20.56 EDT Dream 24-20 Valkyries, 2.48, 2nd quarter 
 Kayla Thornton has knocked down Golden State’s first three-pointer of the night, ending a run of misses from beyond the arc and cutting Atlanta’s lead to four points with three minutes left in the half.
 Canada has been the difference for the Dream, scoring seven of her nine points in the second quarter, including a driving layup through contact for a three-point play.
 Meanwhile, in the mailbag … reader David Bolam is pleased with the venue and tipoff time, but has a bone to pick with the neighborhood:
 double quotation mark At least this game is being played in a decent stadium at a reasonable hour. The neighborhood’s name, though, is the height of plastic, aspirational corporatism. I vote for “The Railyard”.
 The Railyard! Sounds like somewhere a Game 7 ought to be played. We’ll pass it along to the relevant municipal authorities.
 Share 35m ago 20.50 EDT Dream 21-16 Valkyries, 6.39, 2nd quarter 
 Veronica Burton has stopped the bleeding, sinking a pair of free throws with 4min 55sec left in the half to cut Atlanta’s lead to 21-16.
 The Valkyries went more than five minutes without scoring to open the second quarter, missing shot after shot as the Dream put together a 10-0 run. Jordin Canada has six points for Atlanta, while Burton leads Golden State with eight.
 Share 41m ago 20.44 EDT Dream 19-14 Valkyries, 6.39, 2nd quarter 
 Golden State have gone cold. The Valkyries have yet to score in the second quarter, missing their first six shots as Atlanta stretch their lead to 19-14 with 6min 39sec remaining before half-time.
 Reese started the period with a three-pointer, Jordin Canada followed with a driving layup and DeWanna Bonner has just knocked down a pull-up jumper to prompt a timeout from Natalie Nakase.
 It’s an 8-0 Atlanta run and the Valks haven’t touched the twince since the closing stages of the first quarter.
 View image in fullscreen Atlanta’s Angel Reese and Golden State’s Kiah Stokes battle for a loose ball during of Game 7 of the WNBA finals. Photograph: Ezra Shaw/Getty Images Share 43m ago 20.42 EDT Dream 15-14 Valkyries, 9.01, 2nd quarter 
 Angel Reese has picked up where she left off in Game 6, knocking down a three-pointer off a Rhyne Howard assist to give Atlanta a 15-14 lead less than a minute into the second quarter. That’s noteworthy for one big reason: the Dream are a perfect 16-0 when Reese hits at least one three.
 Share 47m ago 20.37 EDT End of first quarter: Dream 11-12 Valkyries
 Not exactly an offensive showcase so far, but no shortage of intensity. Golden State lead 14-12 after a first quarter in which the teams combined to shoot 11-for-33 (33.3%) from the floor and just 1-for-14 from three-point range.
 The Valkyries have been particularly disruptive defensively, recording five blocked shots, including two from Gabby Williams, who has yet to score after missing all three of her attempts. Veronica Burton has carried the offensive load with six points on 3-for-4 shooting, while Kaila Charles has added four points and three rebounds.
 Atlanta, meanwhile, have shot just 29.4% from the field, with Rhyne Howard going 1-for-5 and picking up two early fouls. Allisha Gray leads the Dream with five points, including their only three-pointer.
 After Golden State’s 8-0 opening burst, this has settled into a tense, physical contest. Every basket feels hard-earned.
 View image in fullscreen Golden State’s Kiah Stokes defends a shot attempt by Atlanta’s Jordin Canada during the first quarter of Game 7. Photograph: Ezra Shaw/Getty Images Share 54m ago 20.30 EDT Dream 11-10 Valkyries, 2.16, 1st quarter 
 Atlanta have gone on an 11-2 run to take their first lead of Game 7, with Rhyne Howard’s turnaround fadeaway putting the Dream ahead 11-10 with 2min 16sec remaining in the opening quarter.
 Allisha Gray sparked the comeback with a three-pointer from 27 feet, while Jordin Canada added a driving layup before Howard’s go-ahead basket. The Dream started 0-for-10 from the floor but have made five of their last five shots.
 One early concern for Atlanta: Howard has already picked up two personal fouls.
 Share 1h ago 20.27 EDT Dream 7-8 Valkyries, 3.28, 1st quarter 
 The Dream are finally on the board after going more than five minutes without a point. Angel Reese opened Atlanta’s account with a running reverse layup off an offensive rebound, before Allisha Gray added another basket to cut Golden State’s lead to 8-4. Gray then connects from deep to pull the Dream within one.
 The Valks’ defense has been the story so far, with Gabby Williams already recording two blocks. But Atlanta have bounced back nicely after an icy opening stretch.
 View image in fullscreen Golden State’s Kaitlyn Chen and Juste Jocyte react from the bench during the first quarter of Game 7. Photograph: Ezra Shaw/Getty Images Share Updated at  20.46 EDT 1h ago 20.23 EDT Dream 0-8 Valkyries, 5.43, 1st quarter 
 A nightmare start for Atlanta on Halloween night! The Valkyries have scored the game’s first eight points, forcing Karl Smesko to call timeout less than a minute before he’d get one for free.
 Golden State have been relentless defensively, with four different players recording blocked shots already. Kiah Stokes converted a putback layup before Kaila Charles swatted away a Rhyne Howard jumper, collected the rebound and drew a foul at the other end. Charles made both free throws to bring her tally to four points.
 The Dream are still searching for their first basket more than four minutes into the biggest game in franchise history.
 Share 1h ago 20.18 EDT Dream 0-4 Valkyries, 7.00, 1st quarter 
 A superb defensive start from Golden State, who have held Atlanta scoreless through the opening three minutes. Veronica Burton blocked Allisha Gray’s early attempt before opening the scoring with a nine-foot fadeaway jumper, while Gabby Williams and Kiah Stokes have also come up with blocks.
 Kaila Charles has since added a driving layup off a Williams assist to make it 4-0 with 7min remaining in the first quarter. The Dream have yet to find their offensive rhythm, missing all six of their shots from the floor including a pair of missed threes by Rhyne Howard.
 Share 1h ago 20.11 EDT Tonight’s starting lineups
 Not much longer now. They’ve just announced the starting fives for tonight’s winner-take-all Game 7 of the WNBA finals at Chase Center.
 Atlanta Dream
 No 3 Jordin Canada – Guard
 No 15 Allisha Gray – Guard
 No 10 Rhyne Howard – Guard
 No 00 Naz Hillmon – Forward
 No 5 Angel Reese – Forward
 Golden State Valkyries
 No 22 Veronica Burton – Guard
 No 15 Tiffany Hayes – Guard
 No 1 Gabby Williams – Forward
 No 6 Kaila Charles – Guard/forward
 No 41 Kiah Stokes – Center
 Natalie Nakase’s Valkyries are chasing their first championship in only their second season, while Karl Smesko’s Dream are seeking the franchise’s first title in their fourth trip to the WNBA finals.
 Share 1h ago 20.08 EDT Here’s another measure of just how far the WNBA has come : tonight’s Game 7 is the most expensive ticket in US sports this weekend, according to ticketing analyst Keith Smith.
 The cheapest seat at Chase Center was going for $364, comfortably ahead of Sunday’s Browns-Steelers ($265), Chiefs-Broncos ($264) and Ravens-Bills ($245) NFL games, as well as Saturday’s Florida-Georgia college football showdown ($226).
 Smith notes that the winner-take-all clash between the Valkyries and Dream is on pace to become the most expensive WNBA finals game on record. Not bad for a league that, three years ago, would scarcely have figured into this conversation.
 Share 2h ago 19.54 EDT It’s Ballhallaween and these Valkyries fans understood the assignment. With Halloween falling on the night of the first Game 7 in WNBA history, supporters turned out in costumes of all kinds to celebrate outside Chase Center before tipoff. Here’s a look at some of the best outfits from a festive night in San Francisco.
 View image in fullscreen Valkyries fans pose in Halloween costumes at Thrive City outside Chase Center in San Francisco ahead of Saturday night’s winner-take-all Game 7 of the WNBA finals against the Atlanta Dream. Photograph: Heather Diehl/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Decked out in Halloween costumes and lavender accessories, Valkyries supporters dance outside Chase Center before the first Game 7 in WNBA history. Photograph: Heather Diehl/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Golden State fans adjust their purple capes at Thrive City ahead of the Valkyries’ championship decider against the Atlanta Dream on Halloween night in San Francisco. Photograph: Heather Diehl/Getty Images View image in fullscreen A Valkyries supporter shows off her skeleton face paint outside Chase Center before Saturday’s Game 7, with Golden State seeking their first WNBA championship in only their second season. Photograph: Heather Diehl/Getty Images View image in fullscreen A Golden State fan sports the slogan “Game 7 Do or Dyke” painted across their back at Thrive City ahead of the Valkyries’ winner-take-all showdown with Atlanta on Saturday night. Photograph: Heather Diehl/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Halloween meets Ballhalla as costumed Valkyries fans gather at Thrive City outside Chase Center before the deciding game of the WNBA finals on 31 October in San Francisco. Photograph: Heather Diehl/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Golden State supporters dressed in Halloween costumes and the team’s signature lavender gather outside Chase Center before the Valkyries and Dream meet in the first Game 7 in league history, with both franchises chasing their maiden title. Photograph: Heather Diehl/Getty Images Share 2h ago 19.43 EDT How they got here
 A quick refresher on how we ended up here. The Valkyries entered the playoffs as the No 2 seed, looking to build on a remarkable second season in which they established themselves among the WNBA’s elite. Their postseason began with a scare against the seventh-seeded Dallas Wings, who pushed them to a deciding third game before Golden State advanced 2-1.
 From there, Natalie Nakase’s team found another gear. The Valkyries swept the third-seeded Las Vegas Aces in three games in the semi-finals, completing the job with an 87-77 overtime victory to reach the championship series for the first time. They’ve since traded blows with Atlanta through six games, taking a 3-2 lead before Thursday’s defeat denied them a chance to clinch the title on the road.
 Atlanta’s path was more straightforward, at least until the finals. The fourth-seeded Dream swept the fifth-seeded Washington Mystics 2-0 in the opening round before dismantling the eighth-seeded New York Liberty , who had stunned the top-seeded Minnesota Lynx in the first round, in three straight games.
 That sweep sent Atlanta to their first WNBA finals since 2013, with Karl Smesko’s team chasing the franchise’s maiden championship after previous appearances in 2010, 2011 and 2013. The Dream took a 2-1 series lead before consecutive defeats left them facing elimination, only to respond with Thursday’s emphatic 80-69 victory at State Farm Arena.
 Now, after 12 postseason games apiece, both teams stand one win from history.
 Share 2h ago 19.36 EDT Preamble
 One game, 40 minutes and one first-time champion. After six bruising contests, several thousand cross-country miles and a series that has swung back and forth without either side managing to seize total control, the WNBA finals have come down to a Halloween night showdown in San Francisco. The Golden State Valkyries and Atlanta Dream will settle everything tonight at Chase Center in the first Game 7 in league history, with a championship neither franchise has ever won hanging in the balance.
 The Valkyries return home with a chance to complete a remarkable ascent, having reached the brink of a title in only their second season. Natalie Nakase’s team will have the backing of a raucous sellout crowd at Chase Center, where the atmosphere inside the arena known as Ballhalla promises to be particularly festive on Halloween night.
 Quick Guide WNBA finals 2026
 Show Schedule 
 Best-of-seven series. All times US Eastern Daylight Time (EDT). 
 Sat 17 Oct Game 1: Golden State 68, Atlanta 64 
 Mon 19 Oct Game 2: Atlanta 79, Golden State 65 
 Wed 21 Oct Game 3: Atlanta 97, Golden State 71 
 Sat 24 Oct Game 4: Golden State 67, Atlanta 62 
 Mon 26 Oct Game 5: Golden State 64, Atlanta 55 
 Thu 29 Oct Game 6: Atlanta 80, Golden State 69 
 Sat 31 Oct Game 7: Atlanta at Golden State, 8pm (USA/CNBC)
 How to watch 
 In the US, the series will air on NBC, USA Network and CNBC, with all games streaming on Peacock. In the UK, it will be carried by Sky Sports. In Australia, fans can watch through WNBA League Pass, with selected coverage also available through ESPN.
 Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback. But Atlanta have no intention of letting Golden State’s fairy tale have its happy ending. Facing elimination at a lunchtime tipoff on Thursday, the Dream rediscovered their offensive touch just as their title hopes were threatening to slip away, boat-racing the Valkyries 80-69 in a game where the final margin barely hinted at the scale of the hosts’ dominance.
 Allisha Gray scored 23 points, Rhyne Howard added 21 and Angel Reese delivered her fourth double-double of the series as Atlanta buried six three-pointers in a blistering opening quarter and built a lead that ballooned to 25 points before half-time. Golden State, meanwhile, shot just 31.4% from the floor, wasting a 26-point performance from Gabby Williams.
 The WNBA adopted a best-of-seven finals format last year, only for the inaugural edition to end in a four-game sweep. This time, the extended format has delivered the ultimate decider. After six games have left nothing to separate these teams, Halloween night will produce a new champion.
 Share 2h ago 19.08 EDT Bryan will be here shortly. In the meantime here’s a look back at Thursday’s Game 6.
